Does the file's front cover
match the landing page?

Upload the weekly feed — .csv, .tsv or .txt — and check every store's front cover. In this feed the front cover is the HeroImgUrl image (for example Pavilions 2813: weeklyad_2026-11-16_2813?$weekly-ads-emails$). Columns are mapped by header name (CircularURL · HeroImgUrl · SafewayStoreID), the tab-vs-comma delimiter is detected automatically, banner-default rows are set aside ungraded, and Run check grades the file's cover against the front cover on each store's CircularURL landing page wherever that cover can be fetched without Flipp credentials — MATCH / REVIEW / MISMATCH, in batches — and marks the rest COULD NOT RESOLVE for the GitHub checker, never "no cover."

What exactly gets compared — the real Shaw's 4471 pair

The feed's HeroImgUrl is the front-cover image — the cover the file says this store is running. It should match the top slice of the front cover actually shown on that store's landing page, which the checker resolves from the feed's CircularURL. How Run works here: rows are processed in batches with progress streamed above, so a full 1,776-store feed stays responsive. There is no cover column in this feed because there doesn't need to be one: HeroImgUrl is the front cover. For each store the browser (1) loads that cover from its Scene7 URL — http:// cover URLs are upgraded to https:// so they render on this secure page; (2) gets the front cover shown on the store's CircularURL landing page where it can be fetched without Flipp credentials — a cover image carried in the row itself (a CoverURL column, or a CircularURLFirstPage that is an image URL); the preloaded demo's covers were resolved from their CircularURLs on Nov 6; and (3) crops that cover's top slice and compares it with the file's cover using the 8×8 hash — MATCH / REVIEW / MISMATCH. For a Nov 16 feed row, the landing page's cover sits behind the banner's Flipp credentials, and no Flipp access token is in this page — so the browser cannot fetch that cover and the store is marked COULD NOT RESOLVE, never skipped as "no cover": its file cover is verified live, and the results CSV carries the file-cover, landing-page, and store values the GitHub checker needs to resolve the same CircularURL server-side, where the token lives, and grade the pair. Banner-default rows (no store, no cover image) are listed separately below and never graded.

No stores match that filter.

Banner defaults — set aside, not graded

These rows in the feed have no store ID and no front-cover image — they are the per-banner fallback rows (for example SWYdefault). They are excluded from the check and from the verdict counts, and are included in the results CSV as BANNER_DEFAULT so the reconciliation accounts for every row in the file.

How an end user runs it — start to finish

1

Open the link

One public page. Nothing to install, no GitHub, no login. A 21-store validated demo is preloaded.

2

Upload the feed

Pick or drop the week's .csv / .tsv / .txt export. Tab vs comma is auto-detected; columns map by header name (CircularURL, HeroImgUrl, SafewayStoreID). Banner defaults are set aside.

3

Preview every cover

Each store card shows the actual front-cover image loaded live from its HeroImgUrl (http upgraded to https), next to its CircularURL landing-page link — filter by banner or search a store number.

4

Click Run

The check runs in batches with live progress. Each store's file cover is verified live from its Scene7 URL; where the landing-page cover can be fetched without Flipp credentials (a cover image carried in the row, as in the preloaded demo), an 8×8 perceptual hash scores the pair. Rows whose landing-page cover needs the Flipp token report COULD NOT RESOLVE and flow into the results CSV for the GitHub checker — plain image math, no AI service.

5

Act on flags

Eyeball REVIEW pairs, stop the send on MISMATCH, download the report with every URL in it — defaults included.

⚠ The one false-flag to know: the check compares against the flyer live right now. Run it after the circular rolls to a new week and a file cover that was correct at send time will flag MISMATCH. That's why each card shows the flyer's valid dates — and why you run it before the send, while that week's flyer is current.

Perceptual hash, in plain terms

Shrink each image to an 8×8 grid, go grayscale, and write 1 if a square is brighter than average, 0 if darker. That 64-bit string is the fingerprint. Compare two fingerprints by counting how many bits differ — that's the distance. The three examples below are the real validated pairs from your file:

File-cover fingerprint

Red squares = bits that differ from the landing-page cover

Landing-page cover top-slice fingerprint

✓ MATCH — distance ≤ 8
Same cover at a glance. Only a few of the 64 hash bits differ. Ship it.
◐ REVIEW — distance 9–24
Same template, something changed — e.g. 49¢ became 59¢. A human eyeballs it.
✕ MISMATCH — distance ≥ 25
Nearly half the grid differs. Different week's cover. Stop and fix.

Validated Nov 6 with the full Python check (pHash + ORB) on these exact URLs: all 17 ACME stores in your file matched at pHash 2, the 3 Shaw's 49¢ file covers came back MISMATCH at 30–32, and Safeway 2657 landed in REVIEW at 16 — same turkey template, different price. The browser run uses the 8×8 hash alone, so its distances can differ by a few points from the Python pHash; the verdict bands are the same idea.

Where this page can live

Public page (this prototype)

  • End user just opens a link — uploads the week's feed export (.csv / .tsv / .txt) and the browser fetches the front-cover images from their HeroImgUrl URLs and does the computing
  • No Flipp credentials in this page — none stored, none fetched at run time; they live only in the GitHub checker. This page grades pairs whose landing-page cover it can fetch without credentials (the demo rows, or a cover image carried in the feed row) and marks the rest COULD NOT RESOLVE, with every URL exported for the server-side run
  • Best for: anyone on the team previewing and reconciling a feed independently, no login

GitHub / SFMC options

  • GitHub Actions: full two-signal check (pHash + ORB feature matching) with live Flipp cover resolution on a real machine; can pull the feed from SFTP on a schedule
  • SFMC CloudPage: can't decode images itself — it can only be the front door that embeds this page
Preloaded demo: example_feed.csv + demo_49c.csv (Nov 4 feed) — 21 stores, real HeroImage and CircularURL values on every card; thumbnails are snapshots saved from those URLs on Nov 6, with each landing-page cover already resolved. Upload the Nov 16 feed export (1,776 stores + 8 banner defaults) to preview and reconcile the full file: its HeroImgUrl images are the front covers, and Run grades them against each store's landing-page cover wherever that cover can be fetched without Flipp credentials — the rest are marked COULD NOT RESOLVE for the GitHub checker, which resolves the same CircularURLs server-side. No images are sent to any AI service — the comparison is arithmetic on pixels, done in the browser.
